import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The $\frac 1 3$–$\frac 2 3$ conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1/3%E2%80%932/3_conjecture)
-/

namespace Conjecture_1_3_to_2_3

/--
Does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered
contain two elements $x$ and $y$ such that the probability that
$x$ appears before $y$ in a random linear extension is between $\frac 1 3$ and $\frac 2 3$?

The set of all total order extensions is represented as order preserving
bijections $P$ of $1, ..., n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6]
theorem conjecture_1_3_to_2_3 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (P : Type) [Finite P] [PartialOrder P]
    (not_total : ¬ Std.Total (α := P) (· ≤ ·)) (total_ext : Set <| OrderHom P ℕ)
    (total_ext_def : ∀ σ, σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range σ = Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)),
    ∃ x y : P, ({σ ∈ total_ext | σ x < σ y}.ncard / total_ext.ncard : ℚ)
      ∈ Set.Icc (1/3) (2/3) := by
  sorry

end Conjecture_1_3_to_2_3

reformulations.difference: Linear extensions are encoded by order homomorphisms whose range is exactly Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P), without explicitly requiring injectivity. The extension set is universally quantified subject to its membership characterization.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing n = Nat.card P, the interval [1,n] has exactly n elements. Thus a map from finite P with this range is automatically a bijection onto the interval. Monotonicity makes it precisely a rank assignment for a linear extension: each extending total order has one such assignment, and comparing ranks records which element occurs earlier. The membership characterization uniquely determines total_ext. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, range_iff_bijection proves the range-condition ↔ explicit-bijection equivalence, and rank_encoding_iff proves that the quantified-set formulation can be replaced by the explicit rank-bijection set for any property of that set, including the probability bound. Independent Lean proofs also establish finiteness and nonemptiness, so the cardinality ratio is the uniform probability and cannot encounter an infinite-cardinality or zero-denominator default.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the sole declaration. The answer scope, non-totality hypothesis, strict rank comparison, inclusive endpoints, and rational division agree with the sources. Empty and singleton posets are excluded by non-totality; the probability lower bound automatically excludes x = y. Computable rank-enumeration tests give probability 1/2 for the two-element antichain and the expected 1/3 and 2/3 endpoints for the source's three-element example. The scratch file compiles, and its core semantic proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Wikipedia explicitly says the general conjecture remains unsolved, consistent with research open. The reviewed file's hash matches the committed version.
